clue.text: Gradually — how crypto fortune is made?

blocks.note: first meaning: little by little
second meaning, playful: a cryptocurrency fortune is built from bitcoins

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun on Bitcoin: a crypto fortune is made one coin at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for slow, piecemeal progress, and literally describes amassing bitcoins one by one.

clue.text: Talks back when checking explosive urge

indicators.note: something explosive gets blown apart, so the letters of the following word are scattered
to check is to hold back or restrain, so the outer word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: as in 'as he left' means when he left
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone answers back at the moment they are holding in a violent impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk back is to dispute or contradict, which is what someone who argues does.

clue.text: Group about to appear in Great Bake Off

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be found inside it, so one piece goes within the others
off here means gone bad or out of order, so the combined letters are rearranged

blocks.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some category of people is about to compete on the TV baking show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great British Bake Off is a popular British TV baking contest, so the clue reads as casting news.
explanation.definitionFit: An age bracket is a category of people sorted by how old they are, so a group in a classification.

clue.text: Drinks in midweek? Pass!

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: an animal laps when it drinks with its tongue
mid- asks for the centre of the word week, its two central letters

explanation.surface: Someone offered drinks in the middle of the week declines: 'Pass!'
explanation.definitionFit: Time passes, or elapses; both verbs describe time going by.

clue.text: China has many an ornamental garden

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a conventional 'many'
a garden of rocks and alpine plants

explanation.surface: The country of China boasts numerous decorative gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: China with a capital C looks like the country, but it is the tableware.
explanation.definitionFit: China is porcelain tableware, and crockery is the general word for plates, cups and dishes.

clue.text: Play about Gazan finally getting award

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so just the last letter of the word before is used
about means surrounding, so the first word wraps round the letter

blocks.note: to toy with something is to play with it
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A drama about someone from Gaza wins a theatre prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tony is the American theatre award for Broadway productions, named after Antoinette Perry.

clue.text: French path in South Gironde at first slippery

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the place name is wanted
in places the first piece inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: the compass abbreviation
chemin is the French word for path or way
the opening letter of the department name

explanation.surface: A French track through southern Gironde is slippery underfoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slippery' reads as describing a muddy path, but it means devious.
explanation.definitionFit: A slippery person is shifty and untrustworthy, the same as one who is scheming and plotting.

clue.text: Quick to help the erring player?

blocks.note: first meaning: punctual, done without delay
second meaning: to feed a forgetful actor the line

explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests sport, but here it is an actor who has dried on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning without delay and a verb for supplying a forgotten line from the wings.

clue.text: Disorderly Irish customer frequently in pub

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for Irish
a regular is a customer who drinks often at the same pub

explanation.surface: An unruly Irishman who is a fixture at the local bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorderly things lack pattern or order, which is to say they are uneven or out of line.

clue.text: Character coming before Papa gets 22A award

blocks.note: first meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for O comes just before the one for P
second meaning: the statuette handed out by the Academy

explanation.walkthrough: 22A is ACADEMY, so the second half is an Academy Award. The NATO alphabet runs ... November, ___, Papa, Quebec.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the radio code word for the letter O and the popular name of the film industry's Academy Award.

clue.text: Obscure book — promotional copy?

blocks.note: to blur is to make indistinct
standard abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A little-known book whose cover text is merely advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure book' reads as an adjective and noun; 'obscure' is in fact a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the short persuasive text on a book jacket, written to sell it.

clue.text: Wave to welcome pained daughter? Thick-skinned sort

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in a guest, so the outer word takes the others inside it

blocks.note: a perm is a permanent wave set into hair
aching, sore
standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone waves hello to a hurting daughter and turns out to be insensitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick-skinned' sounds like an insult to a person; it is literal here.
explanation.definitionFit: A pachyderm is an elephant, rhino or hippo, animals named for their thick hides.

clue.text: Restricted way in which sulphur absorbed into volatile nebula

indicators.note: something absorbed into another is taken inside it
volatile means unstable, so the letters will not hold their order

blocks.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An astronomer's note on a gas cloud swallowing sulphur along a constrained path.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus lane is a strip of road reserved for buses, so its use is limited to certain vehicles.

clue.text: Bighead having grand slam of 25, 21D, 10 & 6 first?

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of each of the referenced entries

blocks.note: those entries are EMMY, GRAMMY, OSCAR and TONY; their initials make the showbiz 'grand slam' acronym
the suffix -ist names a person who holds or practises something

explanation.surface: A conceited performer who has won all four major entertainment awards.
explanation.walkthrough: An EGOT is the nickname for winning an Emmy, Grammy, Oscar and Tony; the -IST suffix makes someone holding one an EGOT-IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A bighead is a conceited, self-centred person, which is what an egotist is.

clue.text: N European in country who's wrecked individual enterprise?

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the country name
something wrecked is smashed up, so the letters are put back together differently

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for European
the Gulf state
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A northern European living abroad whose solo venture has collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-man show is a performance or business run by a single person, an individual's undertaking.

clue.text: Dog tucking right into food

indicators.note: tucking something away tucks it inside something else
into places the preceding letter inside the following word

blocks.note: tack is old slang for food, as in hard tack
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A dog is gobbling its dinner straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like the animal tucking in, but it is the verb meaning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, the same as tracking them.

clue.text: 'Queen dead' a lie possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters among many

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rumour that the monarch has died may be false.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide was the queen consort of William IV, after whom the Australian city is named.

clue.text: Latest information unknown: work for MI6?

blocks.note: the SP (from 'starting price') is British slang for the latest information
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: No current news is available: is that the intelligence services' business?
explanation.walkthrough: MI6 is Britain's foreign intelligence service; the answer is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Working for MI6 means gathering secret intelligence, which is to spy.

clue.text: Calmness before stupid coming through Surrey's borders?

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, so only its first and last letters are used
to come through a place is to pass inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the county name
ere is a poetic word for before
a nit is a fool, a stupid person

explanation.surface: Peace and quiet ahead of an idiot driving through the edges of Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south-west of London. 'Stupid' is used as a noun, a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: Serenity is a state of peaceful composure, the same thing as calmness.

clue.text: False strokes producing boundaries

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket, mis-hits off the side of the bat
second meaning: borders, rims

explanation.surface: Lucky mishits in cricket still bring fours.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a boundary is a shot reaching the rope; here it is simply the margin of something.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an edge is a stroke off the bat's side, and edges are also limits or margins.

clue.text: Perhaps on air one refused a farewell

indicators.note: a thing refused is turned away, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: say, as in 'say, ten people', means perhaps
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A broadcaster on air may have declined to say goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Sayonara is the Japanese word for goodbye, used informally in English as a parting word.

clue.text: More on passing through eighteenth entrance?

indicators.note: something passing through another goes inside it

blocks.note: a gate is a way in
R is the eighteenth letter of the alphabet
re means about or on, as in letters

explanation.surface: A golfer heads on through to the gate by the eighteenth hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Greater means larger in amount or degree, which is what 'more' expresses.

clue.text: Elegist covering very short distance gets award

indicators.note: covering means lying over and around, so the poet's name surrounds the distance

blocks.note: Thomas Gray wrote the famous Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
mm is the abbreviation for millimetre

explanation.surface: A mourning poet who travels a tiny distance wins a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grammy is the American music industry's annual award.

clue.text: Day came for reforming educational institution

indicators.note: reforming means shaping anew, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The day arrived for overhauling a school.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school or college, and in Britain a type of state-funded school.

clue.text: Poet, Italian flower, died around lake

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the preceding letters wrap the next one

blocks.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Arno flows through Florence
standard abbreviation for died
standard abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A poet, like an Italian bloom, perished by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' looks like a bloom, but read it as 'flow-er', something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Arnold was a Victorian English poet, author of Dover Beach.

clue.text: What Cockney repairman does? Makes alterations!

indicators.note: Cockney speakers famously drop the h at the start of words

blocks.note: what a repairman does: he mends

explanation.surface: A question about a London handyman's work, answered with the fact that he changes things.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner whose accent drops initial h, so 'he mends' comes out as ''e mends'.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct or revise a text, so it makes alterations.

clue.text: Soon pressing flesh, leader from Mycenae? That's him

definitions.text: Soon pressing flesh, leader from Mycenae? That's him

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
pressing means squeezing round, so the first word encloses the others

blocks.note: anon is an old word for soon
game is the meat of hunted animals
the first letter of the city's name

explanation.surface: A Greek king of Mycenae shaking hands with people: that's the one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer too: 'leader from Mycenae' is its king.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the legendary king of Mycenae who led the Greeks at Troy.

clue.text: Award or prize judge denied?

indicators.note: something denied is refused entry, so that letter is not allowed in

blocks.note: to prize (prise) open is to jemmy, using a burglar's crowbar
standard abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: Is this an award, or a prize the judges refused to give?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' reads as a trophy noun; it is a verb, to lever open.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmy is the American television industry's award.

clue.text: Flying V?

blocks.note: surface reading: the Gibson Flying V electric guitar, or a letter shape in the air
setter's reading: the V formation made by a flock of wild geese in flight

explanation.walkthrough: Geese on the wing fly in a V shape, and a flock of them airborne has its own collective noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A skein is the collective term for wild geese in flight, which typically form a V.

clue.text: Bonkers seen with a male brothel-keeper

blocks.note: bonkers is British slang for crazy
taken as written
standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A crazy brothel-keeper spotted with a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A madam is a woman who runs a brothel.

clue.text: Story run about noble's unreasonable request

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first pieces go round the next word

blocks.note: a tale is a story
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a lord is a noble; the 's is 'noble is' in the cryptic reading

explanation.surface: A rumour going round about an aristocrat's outrageous demand.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an idiom for a demand that is difficult or unreasonable to fulfil.
